name: Eshton
overview: Eshton is a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as the son of Mehir. The biblical record provides limited information about him, focusing primarily on his genealogical placement within Judah. There are no additional notes or significant narrative details about his life or actions.
namesAndTitles: The name Eshton is a proper name that possibly means 'hen-pecked [husband]' or 'effeminate.' This meaning is derived from the Hebrew context but was not given by God. The name appears specifically in 1 Chronicles 4:11.
familyAndRelationships: Eshton is recorded as the son of Mehir, establishing his direct paternal lineage. Additionally, he is noted as the father of Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah, indicating his role as a patriarch within his family line. These relationships are explicitly mentioned in 1 Chronicles 4:11-12.
scriptureSignificance: Eshton holds significance primarily as a genealogical figure within the tribe of Judah, contributing to the biblical record of family lineage. His mention in 1 Chronicles 4 situates him within the broader context of God's covenant people, emphasizing the importance of preserving genealogical records. While the text does not elaborate on his personal deeds, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of God in maintaining the descendants of Judah.
